newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Broker cools on Sky City.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Broker cools on Sky City.

text.p: Brokers First NZ Capital have tempered their view of Sky City Ltd's earnings prospects for the year to June 1997, analyst Guy Hallwright said on Wednesday.
Hallwright said First NZ Capital had been right at the top end of forecasts with an expected net profit of NZ$47 million.
"I think the rest of the market was around NZ$40 to $44-45 million. Now I think it's about NZ$39 to $44 million. We've come back to the lowish end of that," Hallwright said.
The 1996/7 year will be the casino operator's first full year of operations, having opened its doors in February.
"But really we are guessing an awful lot because we don't know what the seasonal patterns are. Nobody does," Hallwright said.
The February to June period was not going to be a reliable indicator for the current year.
"All you can say is that there has been a slight softening of numbers over the last couple of months.
"Looking at that and looking at the assumptions behind the NZ$47 million, it seemed prudent to come back from there. It's not a huge downgrade, not a big sell," Hallwright said.
In the five months to June, 1996, the company made a net profit of NZ$15.5 million.
Brokers still expect Sky City to comfortably exceed the NZ$36 million profit forecast in the company's listing profile.
Shares in Sky City were sold down 28 cents to NZ$8.05 on Tuesday.
